newsitem.title: USA: Sara Lee sees FY98 plan for double-digit EPS rise.
newsitem.headline: Sara Lee sees FY98 plan for double-digit EPS rise.

text.p: Sara Lee Corp said Thursday it expects its plan for fiscal 1998 will be for a low double-digit percentage gain in earnings per share, although a strong U.S. dollar likely will continue to impact profits.

"We expect to put a plan together (for fiscal 1998) that calls for low double-digit EPS growth," Janet Bergman, vice president, investor relations and corporate affairs, told a teleconference. "A stronger dollar makes it difficult."
Sara Lee earned $0.41 a share in the third quarter ended March 29, in line with expectations and up about 11 percent from $0.37 a year ago. Sales rose 4.6 percent to $4.6 billion.
Analysts said earlier that, if currency rates had been the same as a year ago, third quarter sales would have been three percentage points higher.
Bergman told reporters that Sara Lee does hedge its exposure to changes in foreign exchange rates.
Sara Lee's packaged meats and bakery sales were up 16.4 percent to $1.79 billion and operating income rose 11.2 percent to $99 million in the third quarter.

Within that division, worldwide unit volumes for Sara Lee bakery were unchanged in the third quarter, as strong international unit sales in the United Kingdom and Australia were offset by a weak retail demand for frozen baked goods in the United States.
Bergman said Sara Lee will focus on premium and indulgent products in its frozen baked goods in the United States, and plans to offer some single-serve versions of its products.

Internationally, Sara Lee continues to look for bakery acquisitions, Bergman said. Earlier this month, Sara Lee said it planned to buy the Brossard bakery businesses in France and Italy from Grand Metropolitan Plc.
"We will continue to invest in bakery acquisitions in Euorpe," she added.
